CHIEF COMPLAINT
Yearly physical examination

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Beverly is a 24-year-old female with a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension presenting for her yearly exam. She reports feeling well overall. She began working at a bakery this summer and has been enjoying the job; however, she notes that her proximity to desserts and treats has led to increased snacking and consumption of sweets during work shifts. She acknowledges that her diet has been poor lately due to difficulty resisting temptation at work. She reports taking her diabetes medication as prescribed without any missed doses. Her blood glucose levels have been elevated and fluctuating, which she attributes to her dietary changes. Her blood pressure has remained good despite the blood sugar fluctuations. She is sleeping well with a full eight hours nightly. She denies any suicidal or self-harm ideation.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
No additional concerns beyond those discussed in HPI. Otherwise unremarkable.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Hypertension
Grade 2 systolic ejection fraction cardiac murmur (unchanged)

MEDICATIONS
Metformin 500 mg twice daily
Lisinopril 10 mg once daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recently started working at a bakery this summer. Works in close proximity to desserts and treats.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Well-appearing
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; grade 2 systolic ejection fraction murmur present and unchanged; carotid bruits absent; pulses good
Pulmonary: Lungs clear bilaterally
Neurological: Strength intact and equal; sensation intact to light touch; grips equal and strong
Extremities: No edema; neurovascular examination intact
Neck: No thyromegaly
Overall: Examination essentially normal

RESULTS
Hemoglobin A1C: Elevated
Blood Pressure: Normal/well-controlled
Vital Signs: Stable

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus - Currently suboptimally controlled. Hemoglobin A1C elevated; goal is <7%, preferably <6%. Patient instructed to reduce snacking and additional sweets. Will check fasting blood glucose in the morning and call results in two weeks. No medication changes at this time; will reassess in two months. If control not achieved, will consider adding additional antidiabetic medication.

2. Hypertension - Stable and well-controlled on current regimen. Continue lisinopril 10 mg once daily. No changes at this time.

Follow-up appointment in approximately two months to reassess diabetes control.
